transcript:
Meeting header: Date 2025-08-27 Time 10:00 AM PT Duration about 45 minutes Attendees Alex Chen Redwood AE Priya Kapoor Redwood SE Jordan Lee Atlas CTO Sofia Martinez ML Engineer Ethan Park Infra

Auto-summary: Redwood presented this week's benchmark run results versus Atlas baseline. Main takeaways Redwood p95 improved to approximately 180 ms on the demo model with batching and quantization while the baseline provider p95 was around 420 ms. Redwood sustained throughput approximately 120 rps versus baseline about 85-90 rps under similar payloads. Discussed tuning options for batch size, quantization level, and KV cache. Agreed to run additional experiments with batch 16 and KV cache enabled and to schedule a private staging test using a customer trace.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining quick roll call
[00:04] Jordan Lee: Jordan here Sofia and Ethan are on
[00:07] Sofia Martinez: Hey all
[00:08] Ethan Park: Ethan here
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Hi team Priya from Redwood I'll drive the perf details
[00:14] Alex Chen: Agenda review benchmark numbers tuning changes compare versus your baseline and next steps
[00:21] Jordan Lee: Sounds good go ahead
[00:24] Priya Kapoor: Raw numbers we ran model rdx-13b-fp16-quant on a c5 like harness sequence length 256 payload mix 70 percent short 30 percent long For batch 8 kv cache off we saw p50 48 ms p95 210 ms p99 340 ms throughput about 95 rps After enabling int8 quant continuous batching batch 8 and kv cache warm up we saw p50 32 ms p95 180 ms p99 290 ms throughput 120 rps sustained
[01:02] Sofia Martinez: Sorry can you repeat p95 after kv cache
[01:04] Priya Kapoor: Yes p95 was about 180 ms
[01:07] Jordan Lee: Our baseline on BaselineCloud for same model showed p50 about 70 ms p95 about 420 ms throughput 85 to 90 rps so that delta is meaningful but our traffic has high variance and concatenated tokens increase tail
[01:24] Alex Chen: Two reasons for the win Redwood continuous batching and kernel selection improves GPU utilization and KV cache reduces repeated attention compute Also quantization saves cycles
[01:36] Ethan Park: We saw warm up effects first few minutes tail was higher did you run a warm up
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: We did a 10 minute warm up and measured steady state after 15 minutes With KV cache the warm up is shorter Our measured KV cache hit rate for the run was about 62 percent on your sample traffic
[01:56] Jordan Lee: 62 percent seems plausible How sensitive are numbers to batch size
[01:59] Priya Kapoor: We tested batch sizes 4 8 16 Batch 4 had lower latency but throughput dropped to about 75 rps Batch 16 increased throughput to about 140 rps but p95 rose slightly to about 210 ms unless combined with quantization and kernel tweaks so trade offs exist
[02:22] Sofia Martinez: Did you run the exact same prompt set as our baseline we had mismatch last time
[02:27] Priya Kapoor: We aligned using the sample trace you provided but there were a few long prompts missing We noted differences in the sheet We'll ask for a full 24 hour trace to reproduce fully
[02:38] Alex Chen: Provider differences matter the baseline runtime is different and doesn't expose kernel selection or same KV cache semantics so comparisons need context
[02:49] Jordan Lee: For compliance we need VPC private deployment behavior Any impact to latency there
[02:56] Priya Kapoor: Small network hops can add under 10 ms to p95 in same region Bigger impact is autoscaling cold starts mitigated with reserved capacity
[03:09] Ethan Park: If we go private we will use our GCP fleet Have you validated on GCP A2 A3s
[03:15] Priya Kapoor: We validated on A2 and A10 like shapes Kernel selection adapts quantization path similar We will run targeted test on your instance type during staging
[03:24] Jordan Lee: Where did the biggest wins come from
[03:27] Priya Kapoor: Two wins continuous batching with dynamic windows for GPU occupancy and KV cache for multi turn sessions reduced attention compute by about 40 percent Combined with int8 quant gives best unit cost trade off is small accuracy delta about 0.6 percent on your eval set within tolerance
[03:54] Sofia Martinez: Which quant level int8 or hybrid
[03:57] Priya Kapoor: Int8 with per channel scale we tried 4 bit mixed quant on some layers but that increased variance We leave q8 as default for production
[04:09] Jordan Lee: Baseline quoted different price can we get TCO estimate
[04:14] Alex Chen: I'll include a cost comparison per token and per hour with reserved versus on demand assuming your monthly volume
[04:22] Ethan Park: Baseline runs showed p99 spikes up to 1.2 seconds on longer prompts did you see similar blips
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: We saw p99 spikes rarely above 800 to 900 ms after warm up The spikes correlated with long concatenated prompts not included in shorter tests With full 24 hour trace we can find those patterns and tweak batching windows and pre warming
[04:44] Alex Chen: We can enable adaptive fallbacks to smaller model variants for very long prompts to keep SLAs
[04:50] Jordan Lee: How quickly to spin up a canary with that config
[04:54] Priya Kapoor: We can push a canary in staging within 48 to 72 hours after we have the trace and keys
[05:00] Sofia Martinez: Tokenizer differences changed token counts did you normalize
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: We tokenized with your tokenizer config this week The earlier mismatch was corrected
[05:11] Jordan Lee: Anything else on perf numbers
[05:13] Priya Kapoor: Redwood steady state config batch 8 kv cache int8 p50 32 ms p95 180 ms p99 290 ms throughput about 120 rps Baseline p50 70 ms p95 420 ms p99 up to 1.2 s throughput 85 to 90 rps We included raw logs and histograms in the sheet
[05:33] Jordan Lee: Promising we'll review raw logs
[05:37] Alex Chen: Next steps additional runs batch 16 plus kv cache and private staging test
[05:44] Ethan Park: We'll prepare staging project share keys and a sample VM image
[05:49] Sofia Martinez: I'll send an eval subset for accuracy regression checks
[05:52] Jordan Lee: We'll pick staging run date after we see the sheet
[05:56] Alex Chen: Thanks we'll share the sheet by Friday If no further questions we'll wrap
[06:03] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone
[06:05] Sofia Martinez: Thanks
[06:06] Ethan Park: Thanks
[06:07] Priya Kapoor: Bye all

End of transcript
